::: {.hero-bio}
I am **Emmanuel Hackman**, a PhD student in Computational Science (Mathematics)
at the **University of Southern Mississippi**.

My research sits at the intersection of **mathematical biology**,
**scientific computing** and **numerical analysis**. I develop
physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and numerical methods for forward and
inverse problems in partial differential equations, with a focus on
**neuroscience**: estimating dopamine diffusion and uptake from sparse
electrode recordings in **Parkinson's disease**, and modelling
**glioblastoma (GBM)**. Next, I plan to extend this work to medical imaging,
possibly in 3D.

## What I am working on

My first paper — measurement-aware PINNs that estimate **dopamine diffusion
and uptake** from sparse electrode recordings — is submitted and under review.
I am now extending it to counterfactual inference (how would dopamine respond
to an intervention such as transporter blockade?) and to nonlinear
Michaelis–Menten uptake, and modelling glioblastoma (GBM).
See [Research](research/index.qmd) for details.
